record_title: Harmonic equilibrium bias and a one-gradient covariance obstruction for randomized ULMC
provenance: Analytic stationary-second-moment consequences of the RMM, ALUM and newly proposed LC-REI predictor-corrector formulas in arXiv:2609.20713, compared with prior randomized-midpoint stationary-bias and Langevin invariant-measure literature.
limitations: The theorem is for a scalar quadratic target and sufficiently small step size, and concerns stationary second moments rather than the full generally non-Gaussian invariant law. It does not rank transient strong error, general-target Wasserstein error, mixing time, or implementation cost. The continuous predictor-noise interpolation is analytic; only the source endpoint methods are established algorithms. Originality is to the best of our knowledge, with contemporaneous follow-up risk because LC-REI is newly introduced.
